newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech coalition agrees to change cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Czech coalition agrees to change cabinet.

text.p: Leaders of the three parties in the ruling Czech coalition agreed on Wednesday to change the makeup of the cabinet, but there was no agreement on which positions would be affected, the Czech news agency CTK reported on Wednesday.

It quoted a brief joint statement of leaders of the three parties in the centre-right coalition as saying a late night meeting between them had ended in an agreement that a change in the composition of the cabinet was necessary.
Czech coalition agrees to change cabinet

Approval ratings for the government and Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's party have fallen in recent weeks because of a slowdown in economic performance, some highly publicised cases of financial crime and problems in the health care and education sectors.
The Czech crown has also been hit by worries about political instability. The central bank intervened several times last week to support it.

Czech Radio quoted sources close to the talks as saying that one proposal under discussion was for Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec to replace Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, with the former ambassador to the United States, Michael Zantovsky, then taking over as foreign minister.
This report could not yet be independently confirmed.
